title: Cleaning a binary decider
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $M$ decides $L$ within time $T$, then there exist a finite binary Turing machine $R$ and a natural number $B$ such that $R$ decides $L$ within time $n\mapsto B\bigl(T(n)+n+2\bigr)$.
replaced:
If a finite machine $M$ decides a language $L$ over the binary alphabet within
time $T$, then there exist a finite machine $R$ and a constant $B$ such that $R$
decides $L$ within time $B\,(T(n) + n + 2)$.
